routes.description: Establish that theism provides a more adequate unified account of scientific intelligibility, reliable cognition, objective moral obligation, apparent order, and the broader context of suffering than skeptical naturalism provides.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if its account connects theism to the principal scientific, epistemic, moral, and explanatory facts while answering naturalistic mechanisms, evidential objections, religious plurality, and the challenge from evil without relying on a merely unexplained gap.

motionBridge.description: Show that the combined scientific, moral, and explanatory considerations support theism more strongly than skeptical naturalism.

centralBridges.description: Explain why an orderly and mathematically intelligible universe, truth-directed cognition, and the value of inquiry are expected under a rational creator.
Ground objective moral status and obligation in theism while distinguishing normative authority from evolved feelings or social conditioning.
Defend divine agency as an explanation of established order and functional organization rather than an inference confined to temporary ignorance.
Reconcile suffering with theism or show that the objection requires moral and eschatological premises that the theistic account can coherently supply.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Connect the historical emergence of modern science to theological commitments about an ordered, knowable, and worthwhile creation.
Specify what observations or comparative explanations may count for theism despite alternative natural or advanced-agent interpretations.

routes.description: Establish that public evidence, testable natural mechanisms, and empirically informed morality explain the relevant phenomena without a divine hypothesis, while suffering and underdetermination count against traditional theism.
routes.successCriteria: The route succeeds if natural inquiry remains adequate for science, cognition, origins, design, and morality; if proposed divine explanations lack discriminating support or specificity; and if theism does not resolve the evidential challenge posed by innocent suffering.

motionBridge.description: Show that the relevant evidence and explanatory methods support skeptical naturalism at least more strongly than the proposed theistic account.

centralBridges.description: Require publicly reproducible, discriminating evidence and causal mechanisms before treating supernatural agency as an explanation.
Account for apparent design, cognitive reliability, and possible cosmic origins through testable or provisionally investigated natural processes.
Explain moral knowledge and obligation through facts about sentient flourishing, reciprocity, cooperation, reasoning, and empirically studied human nature.
Establish the evidential tension between extensive preventable innocent suffering and a deity possessing perfect goodness and unlimited power.

subsidiaryBridges.description: Separate scientific validity from the religious identity of early investigators and address the specificity problem created by competing religions.
Identify how unfalsifiable qualifications, asymmetric attribution, or appeals to unknown causes limit the explanatory content of the God hypothesis.

sections.title: Scientific Intelligibility, Cognition, and Historical Origins
sections.rationale: This issue tests whether the order of nature, human access to truth, the value of inquiry, and the historical rise of science receive a distinctive theistic explanation or are adequately grounded by universal scientific practice and evolved cognition.

sections.title: Design, Cosmic Origins, and Natural Mechanisms
sections.rationale: This issue covers the competing explanations for functional complexity and cosmic origins, including divine agency, evolutionary processes, causal regress concerns, unsettled cosmology, and the permissibility of withholding conclusions while inquiry continues.

sections.title: Evidence, Falsifiability, and Explanatory Method
sections.rationale: This issue determines what could discriminate supernatural agency from natural or advanced-agent alternatives, whether theistic explanation supplies causal content, and whether either framework improperly fixes its conclusion regardless of possible observations.

sections.title: Objective Morality and Human Moral Status
sections.rationale: This issue addresses whether moral truth and binding obligation require divine grounding or can arise from reason, reciprocity, flourishing, cooperation, moral psychology, and social inquiry, including the distinction between explaining moral beliefs and justifying them.

sections.title: Evil, Innocent Suffering, and Theistic Coherence
sections.rationale: This issue bears directly on whether preventable innocent suffering conflicts with a perfectly good and powerful God, whether the objection presupposes objective moral standards, and whether a wider theistic account of suffering and death changes that conflict.

chunk-001:c003.proposition: Christian theological commitments about an orderly and knowable creation motivated pioneers of the scientific revolution and contributed causally to modern science's emergence.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-05.proposition: Theistic explanation need not infer God from temporary ignorance because it can appeal to established knowledge and the intelligible order of nature as a whole.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-06.proposition: The question of who designed the designer does not defeat biological design reasoning because ordered functional composition is attributed to organisms but not likewise attributed to God.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-07.proposition: The problem of evil presupposes an objective moral law applicable even to God, creating a grounding burden for an atheist who uses suffering to argue against theism.

chunk-003:c003-04.proposition: Because unguided natural selection selects for reproductive survival rather than truth, theism better explains the reliable cognition required for scientific knowledge.

chunk-003:c003-05.proposition: A method that reclassifies every apparent divine act as advanced alien technology makes God's existence unknowable by design and cannot discriminate theological evidence.

chunk-004:c004-02.proposition: Biological wiring and social teaching can causally explain moral convictions but cannot establish that the conduct condemned by those convictions is objectively wrong.

chunk-004:c004-08.proposition: Biblical creation and modern scientific findings can be reconciled through Christian traditions that use observation and experiment to discover how God ordered nature.

chunk-004:c004-10.proposition: Appeals to flourishing and autonomy do not by themselves justify those norms, whereas creation in God's image supplies humans with a distinctive moral status.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-04.proposition: Theism remains coherent amid suffering because death need not end a person's story and an afterlife can change the total context of apparently final earthly harms.

chunk-001:c010.proposition: Extensive preventable suffering and death among innocent children conflicts with the joint claims that God is all-powerful and wholly good.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-01.proposition: A God hypothesis that treats favorable outcomes as confirmation while insulating every unfavorable outcome from disconfirmation lacks discriminating explanatory content.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-08.proposition: Scientific findings are publicly reproducible across religious cultures, whereas religious beliefs vary by place and time, so Christianity is not what validates scientific inquiry.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-09.proposition: Darwinian natural selection supplies a bottom-up mechanism by which apparently purposeful, complex biological organs can arise through cumulative gradual change without an intelligent designer.

chunk-002:chunk-002-candidate-10.proposition: Evidence for human makers of artifacts does not establish a cosmic maker; unresolved origins warrant testable inquiry and suspended judgment rather than an unsupported supernatural inference.

chunk-003:c003-06.proposition: Successful measurement, prediction, and spacecraft navigation provide empirical evidence that evolved human faculties increasingly represent and track an external reality.

chunk-004:c004-04.proposition: Love, promise-keeping, reciprocity, social cooperation, and the survival and flourishing of sentient beings provide secular reasons for binding moral conduct without divine commands.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-03.proposition: The consoling prospect of reunion after death does not answer suffering unless it is true, and incompatible religious afterlife accounts intensify the need for supporting evidence.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-05.proposition: Current cosmology does not require a divine first cause because quantum events may be uncaused and the universe may have deeper or eternal physical antecedents, while its origin remains unsettled.

chunk-005:chunk-005-candidate-07.proposition: Rejecting absolute or religious moral ontology does not entail relativism because social science can discover real truths about human nature, moral dispositions, and behavior-regulating institutions.
